bib.title: Empowering Large Language Model Agents through Action Learning
bib.venue: Published as a conference paper at COLM 2024

question: Can an LLM agent learn from trial and error by creating and iteratively revising its own actions (Python functions) on a few training tasks, so that it performs better on unseen tasks of the same type?
hypothesis: The limitation of language agents lies in the integration of planning with the action space, so an adaptable, learned action space unlocks latent planning capability.
contributions: Propose the action learning framework by generating and updating learnable actions, enabling a customized action space that better fits the LLM's planning capacity.
LearnAct uses Python functions as new actions and an iterative strategy where the LLM refines the available actions from errors in failed tasks.
Experiments show LearnAct learns action spaces within a few trials and outperforms SOTA agents by a significant margin.

method.summary: LearnAct has an LLM learner (GPT-4) create high-level actions as Python functions over the basic actions, then repeatedly run an Act agent on 3 training instances, pick a failed case with an action error, and let the learner either update a function or write a note on its description. K=4 candidates are sampled per iteration and the best by success rate plus step accuracy is kept. At test time the agent is a plain Act agent with the learned action space and instructions.
method.task: LLM agent sequential decision making: Robotic Planning (Gripper, Blockworld, Barman, Tyreworld) and AlfWorld

datasets.name: Robotic Planning (AgentBoard / LLM+P implementation)
datasets.split: 3 randomly selected instances per task for training, remaining instances for test
datasets.source: Ma et al. 2024 AgentBoard; Liu et al. 2023 LLM+P

datasets.name: AlfWorld
datasets.split: 3 randomly selected instances per task for training, remaining for test; six task types (Put, Clean, Heat, Cool, Look, Put 2)

other.use: learner F for action creation/improvement (also for Reflexion and Voyager learning) and test-time agent
test-time agent only; GPT-4 is its learner

inference.samples: Sampling number K=4 candidate action revisions per learning iteration; each experiment conducted three times per task and averaged
inference.prompting: Act agent format (instruction, goal, history); a single in-context example provided to LearnAct and all baselines; CodeAsPolicy and Voyager action creation use the identical code example

parameters.stop_rule: until all training instances solved with no action errors or maximum optimization steps exceeded
parameters.max_iterations: not stated as a single value; Fig 3 sweeps 1 to 4 iteration steps (read from Fig 3), best at about 2

metrics.name: task success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of test instances solved (binary outcome reward), averaged over three runs

metrics.name: action success rate / calling rate
metrics.definition: Fig 3 left: frequency of use and accuracy of learned actions before vs after learning

metrics.name: pstepacc
metrics.definition: ratio of successfully executed actions to total steps taken by the agent (used in the selection score)

eval.protocol: Learn on 3 training instances per task, report test-set success rate, mean of three runs; temperature 0.0; no significance test or variance reported.

prompts.where: Appendix A.4, Figure 4 (continues with basic action example, created action example)

prompts.purpose: Action learning (error analysis and Update or Plan choice)
prompts.text: The high-level steps are executed but failed. Please analyze why the execution failed, and give one of the following improvement: Update, Plan.
Now here are some Python function encompassing multiple basic actions to serve as high-level interface in this task. Please write interface instruction for the given Python function.

limits: Only two domains (Robotic Planning, AlfWorld); both are text-based environments with fixed original action spaces and shared rules between train and test.
Learner is GPT-4 for every agent; the paper says strong model capacity is necessary for learning, and no open model is tested.
Only 3 training instances per task and 3 runs; no variance, confidence intervals or significance tests reported; test set sizes not stated.
Excessive iterations overfit to training cases and misdiagnose the failure cause (Appendix A.6.3, Fig 10), so max iterations must be tuned; best at about 2 per Fig 3.
Learned usage examples are often incorrect yet still help, which the authors note without explanation beyond encouraging use.
Reflexion was adapted to a train-test setting and Voyager reimplemented after Wong et al. 2023, so baselines differ from the originals.
Abstract's 32% over ReAct+Reflexion is relative, not absolute points.
Code, data and weights release not stated.

terms.definition: learning to expand and iteratively refine the action space of a language agent, with newly learned actions as Python functions
create initial action functions plus descriptions and usage examples; pick error-inducing steps from failed training runs; fix by function update or by writing a note

lineage.note: Act agent is the test-time agent format; ReAct adds Think action
verbal policy learning, adapted to train-test setting
code skills as actions; reimplemented as Wong et al. 2023 without curriculum
